metaDescription: Eureka cordless sticks, a self-emptying model and a vacuum mop compared by weight, floor sensing, battery swap and upkeep so you match the model to your home.
expertTake: The Eureka ReactiSense NEC451BL is the most capable stick in the family, with floor sensing and a 350W motor. The RapidClean Pro NEC280TL is the value pick at about 5.3 pounds. Skip the family if you want a sealed allergy design or a premium-brand battery platform; these sticks are good light cleaners, not flagship machines.
introParagraphs: This maker's cordless range is built around light weight and simple controls rather than flagship power. The sticks span a basic converting model, a pet-focused line, a sensor-equipped flagship, a self-emptying version and a wet-dry mop.

Choosing within the family is mostly a matter of matching features to the job: floor sensing for mixed homes, a self-emptying station for people who dislike handling dust, and a spare battery plan for larger floors. Weight and battery swap matter more than headline numbers.

products.name: Eureka ReactiSense 350W NEC451BL anti-tangle stick, 60 min

specList.label: Sensing
specList.value: Detects dust level and floor type

specList.label: Brush
specList.value: Anti-tangle brushroll with fins and comb strips

products.description:
ReactiSense is the family's flagship because it thinks. Sensors detect dust levels and floor type and adjust the power automatically, so you spend less time reaching for a mode button and the battery is spent where the floor needs it. A 350W motor and an anti-tangle brushroll with fins and comb strips cover carpet and hard floors.

The sixty minute figure is the maker's rating at the lowest power, so expect less when the sensors raise the power on carpet. Compared with the RapidClean Pro NEC280TL it adds sensing and more motor, but it is heavier, and compared with the Stylus Elite it lacks the self-emptying station.

Ownership is the usual routine plus the sensors. Wipe the sensor windows with a dry cloth, rinse the filter monthly and check the fins and comb strips for packed hair. Eureka sells batteries and filters for the line, so confirm the pack for this model before you rely on it for years. When the sensors raise the power on a rug, the motor note changes, and that is a cue rather than a fault; if the pitch stays high on a bare floor, the sensor window may be dusty, and a wipe usually puts the behavior right. Avoid vacuuming with the head resting against a dark skirting board, which can fool the dust sensor into a high-power mode.
products.bestFor: Mixed floors where the machine should adapt its power on its own.
pros: Sensors adjust power to dust and floor
cons: Costs more than the basic models

products.name: Eureka Stylus Elite NEC490BL with self-emptying station

specList.label: Station
specList.value: Holds up to 3 liters of debris

products.description:
The Stylus Elite is the family's answer to handling dust. Dock the stick and the Clean Station empties the bin into a three liter container, so you touch dirt only when the station is full. A 350W motor, three cleaning modes with runtimes of 15, 40 and 60 minutes and a removable battery cover carpet, hardwood and tile.

Compared with the ReactiSense it adds the station and a removable battery, but gives up the floor sensing. The three liter capacity is generous, which means emptying the station is an occasional job rather than a weekly one.

The station has its own upkeep: wipe its intake and seals, replace the bag or empty the container on schedule, and give it space on the floor. Rinse the stick's filter, clear the roller and keep a spare battery in mind, since the pack detaches. The docking motion matters: seat the stick firmly until it engages, because a half-seated stick leaves the bin partly full and the station running for nothing, and listen for the evacuation burst when you dock, which is the quickest way to know the system is working.
products.bestFor: Households that dislike handling dust and want a spare battery.
pros: Three modes with 15, 40 and 60 minute runtimes

products.name: Eureka RapidClean Pro 250W NEC280TL, 5.3 lb stick

specList.label: Runtime
specList.value: Up to 40 minutes in eco mode

products.description:
The RapidClean Pro is the family's best expression of light weight. At about 5.3 pounds with a 250W motor and three power modes, it is simple to use and easy to carry, and LED headlights show dust under furniture.

The forty minute rating is the eco figure, and the maximum mode gives only a short burst on the sister model. Against the ReactiClean NEC410BK it is a touch lighter but has a non-removable focus on the standard pack, so check the battery plan, and against the ReactiSense it has no sensing.

Rinse the filter monthly, check the brushroll ends and keep the contacts clean. It is the model to buy when weight and simplicity are the priority. Because it relies on a single brushroll design and a modest motor, stick to the middle mode on rugs and keep the highest mode for a short burst, and expect that a thick rug will take more passes than a flagship would, which is a fair trade for a machine that weighs little more than a large broom.
products.bestFor: Light daily cleaning with pets and hard floors.
pros: About 5.3 pounds, light in the hand
cons: Eco runtime is the headline figure
Smaller bin than the sensor models

products.name: Eureka ReactiClean 200W NEC410BK, 5.5 lb, swap a spare

specList.label: Runtime
specList.value: Up to 50 minutes, about 1,345 sq ft in low mode

products.description:
What sets the ReactiClean apart inside this family is how openly it plans for a second battery. The maker sizes one charge in terms of floor area, roughly 1,345 square feet in the lowest mode, and then tells you to click in a spare for the rest of the house. That framing suits a larger home better than a bare minutes figure does.

A brushless motor and a tangle-resistant brush handle the work, and the whole stick weighs about 5.5 pounds, which keeps it comfortable for a full floor plan. Next to the RapidClean Pro it is a little heavier but has the detachable pack, and next to the Stylus Elite it skips the docking station and costs less, so it is the middle path for anyone who wants swappable power without a bulky base.

Buy the spare at the same time as the stick, label the two packs and alternate them so they age together. Wipe the contacts every few months, rinse the filter monthly and treat the 20.3kPa figure as the maker's own claim, not something to compare with another brand. When one pack finally weakens, keep it for short jobs and rely on the newer one for the long ones, which stretches the useful life of both.
products.bestFor: Larger floors that need a swappable pack.
pros: Detachable battery with a clear spare plan
cons: Spare battery is a separate purchase

products.name: Eureka NEW400 cordless wet-dry vacuum mop, self-propelled

specList.label: Tanks
specList.value: Dual tank, clean and dirty water separate

products.description:
This is the family's odd one out and the one to buy if hard-floor mopping is the real job. A self-propelled function means the machine helps drive itself, which reduces the push effort of a heavy wet unit, and a dual-tank system keeps clean and dirty water apart.

It vacuums and washes at the same time, with a self-cleaning system for the roller. Compared with the cordless sticks here it is a different tool: it will not clean carpet, but it handles sticky floors that a dry stick cannot.

Empty both tanks after each use, run the self-clean and let the roller dry. Replace the roller and filter on schedule, and confirm that parts are sold. Use only the cleaning solution the maker recommends, because the wrong detergent foams in the dirty tank and can trigger the full sensor, and wring out or air-dry the roller between uses so it does not sour. Keep the machine out of sunlit windows, where the tanks can warp and the roller dries brittle.
products.bestFor: Hard-floor homes that want a mop rather than another stick.
pros: Dual tanks keep clean and dirty water apart
Vacuums and washes in one pass
cons: Roller and tanks need regular care

products.name: Eureka NEC101 lightweight cordless stick, converts to hand vac
products.description:
The NEC101 is the family's plain converting stick: about five pounds, low and high power settings and a five-stage filter. It converts to a handheld for stairs and upholstery.

It lacks the tangle-resistant roller and the sensing of the newer sticks, so hair needs more attention and carpet is a secondary job. Compared with the RapidClean Pro it is simpler and older, which makes it a basic option for light use.

Rinse the filter, clear the roller and confirm that a replacement pack is sold, since this is an older design. For a small flat with bare floors it does the job. A roller without an anti-tangle design needs a monthly look at the ends, so keep a small pair of scissors beside the charger, and use the handheld conversion for stairs and the car, which is where this simple model earns its keep for owners who have a stronger vacuum for the main floors.
products.bestFor: Small flats with bare floors and light needs.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The ReactiSense NEC451BL detects dust level and floor type and adjusts power, while the RapidClean Pro and NEC101 rely on manual modes. Sensing saves battery and effort in a mixed home. It adds parts that need keeping clean, so wipe the sensor windows, and remember that a sensor can only react to what it detects, so a dark carpet or a dirty lens can make it under-react, in which case switching to a manual mode for a pass is a sensible workaround.

The RapidClean Pro is about 5.3 pounds, the ReactiClean about 5.5 and the NEC101 about 5, while the ReactiSense and Stylus Elite are heavier. Light weight is the family's selling point. Choose the lightest model that has the features you need.

The Stylus Elite station holds up to 3 liters of debris, so you touch dirt only when it is full. The station takes floor space and adds a part that can fail. It suits people who dislike handling dust, and it also benefits anyone with allergies, since the bin is emptied inside the station rather than into the air, though the station itself must be emptied eventually, so plan to do that outdoors into a bag.

The ReactiClean quotes about 1,345 square feet in low mode and then swap in a spare, and the Stylus Elite has a removable battery. A swappable pack extends a stick's life. Confirm the spare is sold before you buy, and prefer the pack that the maker lists by model number, because a generic third-party pack that fits physically may not communicate correctly with the charger and can cut runtime or refuse to charge.

The ReactiSense uses fins and comb strips, the RapidClean Pro a tangle-free roll and the NEC101 a plainer design. Hair wrap is the common chore. Choose by the hair in your home: fins and comb strips for long hair, a tangle-free roll for pets that shed lightly, and a plainer roller only where hair is not a problem, since the cheapest roller is the one you will be cutting free every week.

The NEW400 vacuums and washes in one pass with a self-propelled drive and dual tanks. It is a different tool from the sticks and handles sticky floors. It cannot clean carpet, so a home with both carpet and hard floors will still want a stick, and the mop is best thought of as a second machine for kitchens, entries and bathrooms where sticky spills are the main enemy.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We ranked on weight and balance, because a stick you can lift comfortably is the one that gets used. The NEC101, RapidClean Pro and ReactiClean are the lightest, while the sensor model and the station model weigh more.

howWeEvaluated.title: Sensing and automation
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at sensors and the self-emptying station. The ReactiSense and Stylus Elite lead.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery serviceability
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked which packs detach. The ReactiClean and Stylus Elite do.

howWeEvaluated.title: Hair handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared brushroll designs. The ReactiSense fins and comb strips score best.

cards.label: Self-emptying station
cards.text: The Stylus Elite empties its bin into a 3 liter container. You handle dust rarely, but the station takes space and adds parts.

cards.label: Plain stick
cards.text: The ReactiSense, RapidClean Pro and ReactiClean have bins you empty by hand. They are lighter and simpler.

howToChoose.note: Choose a station if you dislike dust, a plain stick for light weight.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: An anti-tangle brushroll and a bin that empties cleanly. Check roller ends monthly.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The ReactiSense has fins and comb strips, and the Stylus Elite station keeps shedding out of your hands.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have mixed floors, pets or a large home. The ReactiSense or Stylus Elite automate the work.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have a small home. The RapidClean Pro or NEC101 covers daily cleaning.

maintenance.why: Dust on the sensors confuses floor detection.
A clogged filter cuts airflow. Dry fully before refitting.
Hair wraps the shaft and strains the motor, which shortens runtime. Cut it free over a bin, and spin the roller by hand afterward to confirm it turns without dragging.
A packed station loses pull and leaves the bin dirty.
Packs fade in two to five years.

faq.a: The ReactiSense NEC451BL is the most capable with sensing and 350W. The RapidClean Pro is the better value for light use, because it keeps the light weight and tangle-free roll that define the family and leaves out the sensors and the extra motor that many households do not need.

faq.q: Is the self-emptying model worth it?
faq.a: If you dislike handling dust, yes. The station holds up to 3 liters, but it takes space and adds parts.

faq.q: How long do the batteries last?
faq.a: Packs fade in two to five years. The ReactiClean and Stylus Elite detach, which makes replacement easy.

They are lower-mode figures. Expect much less on carpet or at higher power, and treat the minutes on the box as the best case under ideal conditions rather than a guarantee of what you will see across a lived-in home.
No. It is a hard-floor wet-dry mop and is not designed for carpet.

faq.q: Is Eureka a good brand for cordless?
faq.a: It is a solid mid-tier brand focused on light, simple sticks. This is not a flagship platform, so do not expect the parts depth of the largest brands, but the current sticks have batteries and filters on sale, which is the thing that matters most for ownership.
